A double-edged safety razor. Closest shave I've ever had, and the blades are like $5 for 100 of them. I get horrible razor burn every time I try to use a disposable cartridge razor now.

Meh. I have a DE safety razor (a muhle) and I absolutely hate it. I find shaving with cartridges much much better. It is definitely faster and I get a closer shave.

I find this DE safety bullshit to be akin to a religion.

Everybody's skin is different, so I'm not going to act like a fanatic and say that everybody should get a DE safety razor right goddamn now because holy shit it will change your life. DE shaving is definitely slower (There's a lot of pre-washing involved) and takes time to get the hang of, and not all razors or blades are the same. Seeing as the razors range from $30 to $100+, I can't blame you for not wanting to experiment any further with it.

It's a bummer it didn't work out for you, I can imagine you were pretty disappointed with the results you got. If you do get the urge to try it again one day, try a different brand of blades, and use a facial scrub and moisturizing wash before applying the cream and getting to work. Also, don't shave against the grain, that's a surefire way to end up with a bloody face covered in razor irritation. I apologize if this is all stuff you already knew, but the process is different from using a cartridge razor and it's definitely not as convenient.

I'd wager that 99% of the ideas posted here have been posted in to /r/ideasfortheadmins in one form or another. Reddit has very little pressure to add new features simply for making users happier or giving them more control, because Reddit has virtually no competition. Maybe eventually Voat will change that, but even then developers must be much more careful about releasing changes to sites with very high levels of traffic and much larger databases. When dealing with many users, even small impacts on performance are greatly compounded, and recovering from bugs or corrupted databases can be much more costly. As Voat grows, the developers will eventually have to spend time on scaling and performance, and that may drain resources away from other types of improvement.
